next_step: Send SOC2 report + sub-processor list; share DPA draft; schedule security call week of 2026-03-15
notes:
Lead source: inbound free-trial signup (marketing site).
Initial contact (2026-03-02): AE demo + quick walkthrough of hosted API; product team started small POC.
Customer profile: small SaaS vendor building a support assistant layered on top of their existing ticketing system.
Key ask this stage: early security packet for hosted API — SOC2 Type II report, full sub-processor list, standard DPA with data processing details and retention defaults. Wants to know if Redwood persists user-provided PII and for how long, and whether log-levels include query text.
Quotes from call: "We need something we can hand to procurement/security in the next 2 weeks. SOC2 or equivalent is non-negotiable for initial pilot."
Technical requirements: chat + semantic search. Embeddings to power similarity search across KB. Expected peak traffic for POC: ~15-30 reqs/sec, typical payload small (<1k tokens). 95p latency target for chat responses ~ <300ms (edge target desirable). Cost sensitive; will monitor per-token cost closely during POC.
Model preferences / routing: prefer open models initially (for cost), but willing to route to higher-quality model variants for complex flows. Wants explicit fallback rules (route to smaller model under heavy load).
Security/compliance specifics asked: SOC2 report (latest), sub-processors list (hosting, monitoring, analytics), DPA template (needs data-subject assistance clause), SSO (SAML) for Console, audit logs for token usage, option for data retention policy (default 30 days) and ability to purge customer data on request. Asked about encryption at rest and KMS integration.
Procurement notes: SMB procurement — low friction but security must sign off. Expecting legal review of DPA; timeline depends on receiving SOC2 + sub-processors.
Misc: provided initial integration guide link and quickstart code sample. AE to follow up with security packet. SE (Maya) to join security call to walk through logging/retention details.
Tone: pragmatic, time-boxed (pilot in April), risk-averse on data handling, open to hosted API if assurances provided.
